subject: System Design
title: Read-Heavy vs Write-Heavy Workloads
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Read-Heavy vs Write-Heavy Workloads.

hook.text: A blog has millions of reads per day but only 10 writes. An IoT platform has millions of writes but few reads.

buildup.text: Read-heavy systems benefit from caching, read replicas, and B-tree indexes optimized for lookups.

discovery.text: Write-heavy systems benefit from LSM-tree engines, append-only logs, and minimal indexing.

twist.text: Optimizing for reads often makes writes slower, and vice versa. You can't optimize for both equally.

climax.text: Know your workload's read-to-write ratio before choosing a database. It determines everything.

punchline.text: Know your read/write ratio — it drives every decision.

quiz.question: What is best for write-heavy workloads?
options: B-tree indexes with many read replicas
